resolvedFindings.result: Record-scoped materialized views retain tenant, owner/readers and configured owner-only selection; computed fields use the same policy. Tenant publication is explicit.

Managed-output REFERENCE prerequisites determine creation and reverse deletion order. Live node counts permit dependent-first removal of outputs that own trees; removed roots are excluded from final drain.
Existing local derived-field topological ordering retained and verified, including reversed declarations and rollback.
Initial watch failure retries with bounded backoff and one watcher; reconciliation, partial cleanup, shutdown during retry/attach and actual reconnect pass.
Native null-coalescing precedence was reproduced; generated reverse/inclusive expressions now group operands explicitly.
Record-created prefix formulas use the guarded public reader. System access is checked by a private native function; guests and direct record-helper calls remain denied.
The compiler regression permits existing-identity verification but rejects provisioning and unrelated OAuth sign-in mutations.
The handwritten H7 feasibility adapters now register an explicit duplicate-timestamp policy for both roots. No production code or generated build changed.

Source-derived four-root oracle covers 20 mutation checkpoints, 9 full rollbacks, priced-portion rounding, compound provenance, tenant/currency/source changes, same-time settlement, four tax-input modes and cleanup.

retainedLimitation.observed: The multi-reader a_recipe_compound fixture returned spare, main, spare despite two stored rows. WITH NOINDEX ORDER BY id and unordered scans returned the correct two records.
retainedLimitation.workaround: Explicit WITH NOINDEX ORDER BY id in required-output and delivery-tax snapshots; preserve complete results without deduplication. Carry the same limitation into affected frontend source queries.
retainedLimitation.boundary: A smaller reproduction was inconsistent. No internal engine cause, universal index failure, indexed-performance guarantee or engine upgrade is claimed.

limits: A public aggregate is governed by its declared root or view publication policy; private nodes can make ordered traversal fail.
